//: chan_top is the first multi-clock design here: src_clk_i and axi_clk_i are
asynchronous, crossed only by prim_fifo_async plus a prim_rst_sync per
domain. The constraints that matter are in constraints/chan_top.sdc.
The prim files live outside this repository, in the OpenTitan corpus at
/mnt/d/MyWork/verilog. OpenLane refuses to read files above its working
directory, so the flow is launched from /mnt/d/MyWork - the nearest common
ancestor of both trees - by tools/wsl/87_run_chan_top.sh. Paths below are
therefore written relative to this config file and resolve inside that root.
The dependency list came from tools/wsl/86_chan_top_deps.sh, which walks
prim instantiations transitively rather than guessing.
//CLOCK_PERIOD: 10/32 did not close at the worst corner for a genuinely from-scratch
RESULTS.md). Re-swept against that same real routed netlist's real
parasitics, sourcing constraints/chan_top.sdc unmodified except for the
period values, found no plateau in either clock domain - src=12/axi=48
closes the whole design (worst slack +0.90 ns, TNS 0). This value only
seeds early synthesis-stage estimates; the SDC's own create_clock calls
are what actually govern P&R and signoff.
//DIE_AREA: chan_top synthesises to ~172,790 um^2 of standard cells - about 60x
chan_ctrl, because it carries the async FIFO's storage. 420x420 gave 109%
utilisation and global placement refused to start. 800x800 puts it near
27%, and the 3200 um perimeter leaves room for the wide beat_data/strb and
src_crc buses, which is the other thing that has bitten this flow before.
